data.title: Permethrin (5% cream, 1% creme rinse)
data.body:
_Topicals · III Antiparasitics_

**Class:** Synthetic pyrethroid

## Mechanism of action
- Blocks sodium channels in the parasite's nerve membranes (delays repolarisation) → paralysis and death of mites and lice
- Poorly absorbed (under 2%) and rapidly inactivated by esterases in humans → very safe
- Partly ovicidal

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- 5% cream: scabies (first line), including children over 2 months and pregnant/breastfeeding women
- 1% creme rinse: head lice (pediculosis capitis) and pubic lice
- Crusted scabies (with oral ivermectin)

## Dose & formulations
- Scabies: apply 5% cream to the whole body from the neck down (include scalp, face and ears in infants, elderly and immunocompromised), especially between fingers, wrists, genitals and under nails; wash off after 8–14 h; repeat after 7 days
- Treat all close contacts at the same time; wash clothes and bedding in hot water or store in a sealed bag for 72 h
- Head lice: apply 1% rinse to washed, towel-dried hair for 10 min, rinse; repeat on day 9–10; wet-comb to remove nits

## Adverse effects
- Burning, stinging, itch (post-scabetic itch may last 2–4 weeks — not treatment failure)
- Contact dermatitis (rare; cross-reaction with chrysanthemum/ragweed)

## Contraindications
- Hypersensitivity to pyrethrins/chrysanthemums; infants under 2 months (5% cream)

## Pregnancy & lactation
Safe — first choice in pregnancy and breastfeeding.

## Viva points
- Drug of choice for scabies
- Apply neck down (whole body in infants and elderly), 8–14 h, repeat after 1 week
- Treat contacts simultaneously
- Itch persisting 2–4 weeks is expected

_Sources: Wolverton 4e ch.44 (Topical antiparasitic agents); Khopkar ch.21. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
